briefing.opening: Good morning. Welcome to the climate briefing for August 12, 2026. Today, we will provide a comprehensive overview of the escalating global climate crisis and the various domestic and international efforts being made to address it.

sections.title: 🔴 Escalating Climate Crisis and Global Impacts
sections.content: News reports today warn of a deepening global climate crisis. In the Western United States, severe snow droughts are occurring, while across Asia, including Korea, record-breaking heatwaves are causing immense damage to agriculture, with potatoes reportedly 'melting like boiled potatoes' in the ground [46, 73]. Domestically, unpredictable rainfall patterns have exacerbated droughts, leading to regions reporting 0% reservoir levels. Emergency situations persist, with a national firefighting mobilization order issued to provide water support due to extreme drought [11, 15, 44]. Furthermore, extreme heat is creating 'inhumane' conditions where nurses are collapsing, and in the UK, wildfires are raging, leading to considerations of banning disposable barbecues, posing direct threats to human lives and the environment [67, 71]. These climate changes are raising concerns that droughts on the other side of the world could impact Korea's export-dependent economy, exhibiting complex patterns that simultaneously cause both drought and heavy rainfall [8, 60].

sections.title: 🌱 Domestic and International Cooperation and Adaptation Efforts for Climate Action
sections.content: Amidst this crisis, positive domestic and international movements to address climate change continue. Korea and ASEAN have held environmental and climate change dialogues, agreeing to strengthen joint responses, including methane reduction cooperation and air pollution countermeasures [1, 4, 9]. Local governments in Korea are pursuing specific plans for climate change adaptation; Sangju City is establishing a basic plan for crop development in preparation for climate change and promoting a major shift in crops and varieties, while Anseong City is recruiting trainees for special lectures on future agriculture [2, 5, 6]. Furthermore, several local governments, including Gwangmyeong City, Gyeongnam Province, Changwon City, Jinju City, and Gimhae City, have been recognized and awarded for their carbon neutrality achievements through citizen participation. Yongin City and Damyang County are also actively implementing education and policies for carbon neutrality goals [17, 19, 20, 21, 22]. International adaptation efforts are also ongoing, with Serbia commencing preparations for new climate change legislation and protecting 128 communities from climate change through federal funding [53, 54].

sections.title: 🇰🇷 Accelerating Renewable Energy Transition: Domestic Cases and Achievements
sections.content: Domestic efforts for renewable energy transition are yielding concrete results. Yongin Special City has received the highest rating for four consecutive years in the Renewable Energy Convergence Support Project, promoting renewable energy supply to 134 locations and earning praise for its citizen-centric renewable energy policies [26, 27, 28, 29, 32, 34, 36]. Paju City completed the nation's first 'Public Renewable Energy Plant No. 1,' producing solar electricity and directly supplying it to local businesses, thereby fully launching RE100 support [31, 35, 39]. Public-led solar power projects are also actively underway, with KEPCO KDN and Chungnam Development Corporation planning to expand new and renewable energy to a 300MW scale on idle land in Chungnam and return half of the generation profits to the local community [37, 40, 41, 42]. These efforts demonstrate that the 'Race to Zero' initiative is transitioning from an era of declarations to a stage of 'action' [13].

sections.title: 🌍 International Community's Climate Response Discussions and Challenges
sections.content: The international community continues discussions on the complex issues of climate change. Türkiye is preparing for important international conferences, including holding a COP31 Advisory Committee and strengthening diplomacy ahead of the Antalya UN Climate Change Summit [62, 63]. Ethiopia is also exploring ways to make COP32 a productive summit [51]. Meanwhile, the UK Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs (Defra) has been criticized for insufficient climate adaptation efforts, as it was revealed that only 20 out of 6,600 staff are dedicated to climate adaptation work amidst ongoing droughts and wildfires [52, 69]. Additionally, international scientists are shedding light on various aspects of the climate crisis, such as studying climate change and microplastic pollution during Türkiye's Arctic expedition [66].

briefing.closing: As you've seen in today's briefing, the world faces a severe climate crisis, yet simultaneously, diverse efforts and innovations are underway to overcome it. Only sustained international cooperation and concrete actions, both domestically and internationally, can create a sustainable environment for future generations. This concludes today's climate briefing.
